derived_proposition.name: agent_tree_search_as_weighted_proposal
derived_proposition.base_model: For history h_t, base agent action/chunk law pi(a_t|h_t), environment law P(o_{t+1}|h_t,a_t), and terminal failure indicator H(tau), p(tau)=p(h_0)*product_t pi(a_t|h_t) P(o_{t+1}|h_t,a_t).
derived_proposition.agent_only_proposal: If search changes only agent generation to q(a_t|h_t) and environment transitions remain sampled from P, then W(tau)=product_t pi(a_t|h_t)/q(a_t|h_t). The estimator N^{-1} sum_i W(tau_i) H(tau_i) is unbiased when q has support wherever p(tau)H(tau)>0.
derived_proposition.environment_proposal: If environment responses are also biased or replayed from Q(o|h,a), then W must additionally contain product_t P(o_{t+1}|h_t,a_t)/Q(o_{t+1}|h_t,a_t). If P/Q cannot be evaluated, search alone does not identify unrestricted base-distribution failure probability.
derived_proposition.smc_extension: Prefix cloning/resampling is probability-valid only when ancestor lineage and incremental weights are retained under an SMC proposal/resampling construction. Prefix/KV/environment-state caching is an execution optimization; it is not a probability correction and cannot replace proposal probabilities or weights.
derived_proposition.support_guard: Deterministic pruning that makes q=0 on a base-positive failure path destroys unbiasedness. A base-mixture/support floor can preserve coverage, but should be justified as a support guard rather than assumed efficient because defensive mixtures can waste samples when nominal trajectories do not reach failures.

exact_toy_check.setup: Two-turn toy. Base first action risky/safe probabilities 0.01/0.99. Bad-environment probabilities 0.2/0.001. Conditional final harmful probabilities 0.5/0.1. Search proposal changes first action to 0.5/0.5 and harmful action probabilities to 0.8/0.5.
exact_toy_check.environment_biased_case: If bad-environment probabilities are additionally changed to 0.9/0.01, including both agent and environment likelihood ratios still gives 0.001099; omitting the environment ratio gives 0.00549, about 4.995x the base risk.
exact_toy_check.support_failure_case: If the safe first-action branch is pruned completely, the weighted estimator can recover only 0.001 and misses 0.000099, a 9.01% downward bias in this toy.

new_quantitative_evidence.result: The 2026 preprint directly addresses positive-sample starvation by learning twists through progressively rarer intermediate events and importance-correcting samples from the previous-level proposal. Its abstract and method explicitly distinguish proposal concentration from the base-model target probability.

new_quantitative_evidence.source: State-dependent IS for black-box autonomous systems
new_quantitative_evidence.result: The 2024 work evaluates adaptive state-dependent proposals on four long-horizon sequential systems and reports more accurate failure-probability estimates than Monte Carlo and prior importance-sampling baselines; it is direct precedent for trajectory-space proposal learning in stochastic sequential systems.

On a borehole case around Pf=2.9e-5, the proposed coupled multifidelity subset method used 1,147-1,379 HF calls versus 200,000 for HF subset simulation and 17,000,000 for direct Monte Carlo while reporting similar Pf/COV. On a mechanics case it used 913 HF calls versus 60,000 for HF subset simulation with similar Pf/COV. This supports selective HF correction at conditional rare-event levels, not replacement of the HF target by a learned LF score.

logged_objects: target failure label H or a clearly scoped higher-fidelity target
progress/reaction-coordinate score used for intermediate levels
proposal/search policy q with probability of every sampled agent branch
environment proposal Q and base likelihood P when environment is biased/replayed
importance/SMC incremental weights and final probability estimator
composition_for_replayable_multi_turn_ag.execution_layer: BOA-style batching, prefix caching and chunked tree expansion may accelerate generation and branch reuse, but must sit below the estimator. Cache keys for stochastic replay need enough environment/RNG state to reproduce the intended conditional law; a single stochastic suffix must not be silently counted as multiple independent particles.
composition_for_replayable_multi_turn_ag.proposal_layer: Use state/history-dependent search or learned twists to raise failure hit rate. Multilevel intermediate events are a practical mechanism when final failures are too rare to train a useful proposal directly.
composition_for_replayable_multi_turn_ag.estimator_layer: Use IS/SMC weights defined against the deployment/base trajectory law. Search score, in-budget mass and base-distribution risk remain separate endpoints.
composition_for_replayable_multi_turn_ag.fidelity_layer: A cheap learned evaluator can gate expensive target calls near intermediate/final boundaries, but the HF correction must remain in the probability-estimation path. Cross-field multifidelity subset simulation shows that subset-dependent HF gating can avoid the failure mode where a globally confident LF model never learns deep rare-event boundaries.

negative_or_scope_evidence: BOA is strong evidence for multi-turn trajectory search and efficient prefix reuse, but its reported safety score is tied to a likelihood-bounded searched set; it is not by itself an unrestricted unbiased deployment-risk estimator.
Adaptive Multilevel Twisted SMC is a 2026 arXiv preprint and targets fixed-prompt autoregressive LM outputs, not stochastic tool environments or fully general agents.
A learned rare-event score can improve proposal training while still being misspecified relative to the real target; proposal efficiency does not erase target-label bias.
The multifidelity HF-call reductions come from engineering reliability examples, not an agent-evaluation benchmark. The transfer is a mechanism hypothesis, not a demonstrated agent result.

No direct paper was found in this pass that simultaneously provides BOA-like multi-turn agent tree search, stochastic-environment likelihood accounting, and an unbiased unrestricted deployment failure-probability estimator end to end.
frontier: Find or derive a particle/SMC algorithm for stochastic multi-turn agents where BOA-like priority expansion is converted into an explicit q and every environment branch carries P/Q when necessary.

Test whether adaptive priority queues can be combined with unbiased SMC without hidden selection bias; if selection is deterministic, identify the minimum randomization/support floor needed for unbiasedness or a valid lower/upper bound instead.
Find ML/agent-specific multifidelity evidence where a learned judge is corrected by sparse higher-fidelity labels inside a rare-event estimator, with measured bias/variance and HF-call savings.
Quantify representation-score shift separately from proposal quality: keep target label, reaction coordinate, proposal and estimator as four distinct artifacts.
exact_next_action: Search for priority-resampled particle filters, adaptive SMC or rare-event splitting with nonuniform/adaptive particle selection that preserves normalization-constant unbiasedness. Map its selection/resampling theorem onto a multi-turn agent tree with stochastic environment responses. If no exact theorem permits BOA-style deterministic priority expansion, derive a randomized priority proposal with explicit inclusion probabilities and compare variance against ordinary multinomial/systematic SMC. In parallel, search for agent/LLM multifidelity rare-event evaluation with explicit high-fidelity correction rather than proxy-only scoring.
